summary: large-batch-upload half-open socket leak causing elevated 5xx wave
description: Issue summary: Customer AtlasPay reported a sudden and sustained increase in 5xx responses during a large embeddings upload. Impact: several API calls returned 502/504 to AtlasPay customers for ~45 minutes; concurrent sessions for the tenant dropped and some streaming sessions terminated. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated tenant (AtlasPay) using Dedicated capacity pool D-PROD-07. Initial hypothesis: half-open sockets accumulating on the ephemeral proxy caused accept queue starvation and upstream runtime retries that cascaded to API gateway 502/504s.
timeline: 2026-03-12 09:21 UTC - First alert: AtlasPay dashboard shows 5xx rate spike (from <0.1% to ~7%).
2026-03-12 09:24 UTC - Support engaged; customer reported large embeddings upload (multipart) of ~120k vectors via /v1/embeddings/bulk endpoint.
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Observed increased SYN_RECV / CLOSE_WAIT counts on ephemeral-proxy fleet in us-east.
2026-03-12 09:33 UTC - Autoscaler triggered additional runtime replicas but latency and 5xx persisted.
2026-03-12 09:58 UTC - Temporary mitigation: rate-limited AtlasPay bulk uploads and rotated ephemeral-proxy nodes in the affected AZ.
2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - Error rates returned near baseline after rotation and upload throttling; monitoring left in elevated watch mode.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) As a dedicated tenant, POST a large multipart embeddings upload ~100k-150k vectors in a single request using keepalive connections.
2) Observe ephemeral-proxy accept_queue and socket FD counts while upload streams for ~5-10 minutes.
3) Note increasing CLOSE_WAIT / FIN_WAIT2 counts and incremental upstream 502/504s on the API gateway metrics.
4) Simultaneously trigger a second parallel large upload to amplify the effect.
observed_logs: ephemeral-proxy[proxy-03]: fd_count=23000 accept_queue=8192 CLOSE_WAIT=1163 - high number of half-open sockets recorded
api-gateway: upstream response 502 from runtime-frontend-04: read timeout after hedged retries
serving-runtime[gpu-12]: kernel eviction events correlated with high socket churn and increased pagefaults
kvcache: lock-wait spikes during concurrent prefetch; eviction rate +42%
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: large multipart keepalive uploads hold sockets longer and under certain proxy code paths the sockets are not being fully cleaned on client-side aborts, causing accept queue pressure.

Hypothesis B: combination of high ephemeral-proxy FD usage and runtime backpressure triggers hedged retries that amplify upstream load leading to GPU scheduler contention and occasional OOM protection restarts.
Correlation: healthcheck logs show proxy fd growth preceding API gateway 502 spike by ~30s.

Replication in staging: reproduced with synthetic 120k embed upload and TTFB degraded; staging proxy hit CLOSE_WAIT conditions after ~6 minutes unless client TCP reuses connections with aggressive timeouts.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Applied tenant-level rate limit on /v1/embeddings/bulk for AtlasPay (throttle to 2 concurrent uploads).
2) Issued rolling restart of ephemeral-proxy pods in us-east AZ-1 and cleared socket backlog.
3) Expanded accept-queue size on proxies as immediate safety valve (short-term).
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC - Support (Maya Chen) to AtlasPay CS: acknowledging issue, asking for exact upload manifest and SDK version.
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - AtlasPay provided upload manifest (multipart chunk size 16MB, keepalive=true, SDK v1.3.4).
2026-03-12 10:20 UTC - Support: advised temporary upload throttling and confirmed mitigations in progress.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to add socket lifecycle audit logs in ephemeral-proxy to capture client aborts/EOF and originator IP for replay (PR referenced).
2) Service team to harden proxy: ensure CLOSE_WAIT sockets are reaped within configured grace period and validate keepalive pathological path in proxy code.
3) Add rate-limit guard for very large single-request embedding uploads in the API gateway for Dedicated tenants (policy change).
4) Postmortem to include improved runbook for large-batch ingestion and recommended client SDK options (chunking, connection reuse policies).
comments: Diego Alvarez (Eng): we've reproduced locally; proxied client aborts leave sockets in CLOSE_WAIT for longer than expected on kernel 5.x edge config. Patch in progress to force-terminate after grace TTL. (2026-03-13)

SRE (Priya Nambiar): rolled ephemeral-proxy kernel tunables back to conservative defaults in us-east and applied temporary node drain schedule to replace older nodes. Monitoring shows FD counts trending down. (2026-03-13)

Support (Maya Chen): confirmed with AtlasPay that customer-side upload clients will push a minor SDK update to change chunking behavior and set per-chunk timeouts. Customer appreciated the temporary throttling. (2026-03-13)
Security (Evan Brooks): no evidence of abuse; all uploads authenticated and from legitimate AtlasPay IP ranges. (2026-03-14)
resolution: Mitigation complete: temporary rate-limit and proxy rotation reduced 5xx to baseline. Engineering PR #4521 merged to add CLOSE_WAIT reaper and additional socket diagnostics; longer-term policy change created to limit single-request vector counts for dedicated tenants. Follow-up postmortem scheduled and action items assigned.
follow_up_actions: Owner: Diego Alvarez - complete proxy CLOSE_WAIT reaper rollout to prod by 2026-03-20
Owner: Product - design API-level guardrails for embeddings bulk uploads (max vectors per request) by 2026-04-01
Owner: DX - publish SDK guidance for chunking and timeouts and notify large dedicated tenants.
